task: Fix Node.js OOM during Claude Code session analytics report generation by short-circuiting native session discovery to the requested sessionId before parsing, fixing the unbounded 3650-day discovery window, and preserving Pi /fork family folding under sessionId scoping

component_scope.label: M
component_scope.layers: Workflow (analytics native session discovery/synthesis, consumed by report generation and cost enrichment)

requirements_clarity.label: S
requirements_clarity.gaps: None remaining in the final diff. A code review round found one follow-up defect (CR-001: the sessionId short-circuit broke Pi /fork family folding), which was identified and fixed in a second commit with a dedicated regression test.

technical_risk.label: L
technical_risk.risk_factors: Fixes a production OOM crash on a performance-critical path (unbounded transcript parsing before filtering); the fix interacts with pre-existing Pi fork-folding logic and a prior defect in that interaction (CR-001) was only caught during code review, indicating the scoping change had non-obvious side effects on correctness.
technical_risk.mitigation: Added targeted unit tests pinning the sessionId short-circuit (parses only the matching descriptor, still parses Pi descriptors for fork-fold correctness, zero-parse on no match, no-regression when sessionId absent), the windowDays(undefined vs fromDate) behavior, and a CR-001 regression test asserting the fork continuation still folds into the root when filter.sessionId scopes to the root.

key_reasoning.reason: Fix sits on the exact path that caused a production OOM; it also had a non-obvious interaction with existing Pi /fork fold logic that required a code-review-driven follow-up fix (CR-001), showing the scoping change was not risk-free despite being small.

native-loader.ts is a shared utility consumed by every native agent's session synthesis (claude, codex, copilot-cli, pi, gemini) and by downstream report generation and cost enrichment, so a change here has wider blast radius than its single-file footprint suggests.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M to L: 'Performance as primary concern' — the change directly addresses an OOM crash on a hot/critical parsing path
Component Scope bumped from S to M: 'Touches core shared utilities' — native-loader.ts backs session discovery for all native agents and is consumed by the report and cost-enrichment pipelines
